The equation was balanced by conserving the atoms of every element.

Worked solution: every row of the species matrix $\mathbf{A}$ is a conserved quantity (O, S, Cu, Zn), every column a species (reactants negative, products positive). The smallest positive integer coefficients $\nu$ with $\mathbf{A}\,\nu = \mathbf{0}$ are sought (null space of the matrix).

$M = \sum_i N_i\,A_{\mathrm{r},i} \cdot M_\mathrm{u}$ with $M_\mathrm{u} \approx 1$\,g/mol (relative deviation below $10^{-8}$). The uncertainty combines the uncertainties of the abridged atomic weights (same element fully correlated, different elements independent)~\cite{er-ciaaw2024,er-ciaaw2021}.

For the solution 0,1 M CH3COOH the proton balance (charge and mass balance, concentrations instead of activities) at 25\,\textdegree C gives $\mathrm{pH} = 2.88$; $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{w} = 13.995$, neutral would be $\mathrm{pH} = 7.00$~\cite{er-harris,er-atkins,er-bandura2006,er-srd46}.
Oxidation numbers follow the IUPAC definition (bonding electrons to the more electronegative partner; Pauling electronegativity)~\cite{er-karen2016,er-redbook2005,er-pubchem_pt}.
Zn ($0 \rightarrow +2$) is oxidised, Cu ($+2 \rightarrow 0$) reduced; $n = 2$ electrons are transferred per formula conversion.
Net ionic equation (dissolved salts, strong acids and bases as ions, spectator ions $\mathrm{SO_{4}^{2-}}$ cancelled):~\cite{er-atkins}
Half-reactions (balanced with electrons, H$^+$ or OH$^-$ and water):

Standard potentials follow from the Gibbs energies of formation, $E^\circ = -\Delta_\mathrm{r}G^\circ/(nF)$, versus the standard hydrogen electrode ($\Delta_\mathrm{f}G^\circ(\mathrm{H^+, aq}) = 0$, $\Delta_\mathrm{f}G^\circ(\mathrm{e^-}) = 0$)~\cite{er-bard,er-atkins}.
The reaction is spontaneous under standard conditions~\cite{er-codata2022}.
From $\Delta_\mathrm{r}G^\circ$ of the equation as written (phases as in the thermochemistry), $E^\circ = 1.084$\,V.
The limiting reagent is $\mathrm{Zn}$; the extent of reaction is $\xi = 0.09942$\,mol.

Worked solution: for every given reactant $n = m/M$ (or $n = c\,V$, for gases $n = pV/(RT)$); the possible extent is $\xi_i = n_i/\nu_i$. The smallest $\xi$ identifies the limiting reagent; formed are $n_j = \nu_j\,\xi$ and $m_j = n_j\,M_j$.

Atom economy after Trost: mass share of one product in the mass of all reactants ($\mathrm{AE} = \nu_P M_P / \sum \nu_E M_E$)~\cite{er-trost1991}: $\mathrm{ZnSO_{4}}$: $71.8$\,\%, $\mathrm{Cu}$: $28.2$\,\%.

The reaction quantities follow from the standard formation quantities of the species at $T^\circ = 298.15$\,K and $p^\circ = 1$\,bar (Hess's law; $\nu$ negative for reactants)~\cite{er-cox1989,er-wagman1982,er-reed2020}.
The reaction is exothermic and exergonic under standard conditions; $\Delta_\mathrm{r}H^\circ < 0$, $\Delta_\mathrm{r}S^\circ < 0$: enthalpy-driven, spontaneous below $T^*$~\cite{er-atkins}.

$\Delta_\mathrm{r}G^\circ < 0$ only means that the reaction can proceed; it says nothing about its rate. The activation energy does not follow from the equation and the formation data but from kinetic measurements (Arrhenius plot).

Where the table gives no $\Delta_\mathrm{f}G^\circ$, it is calculated from $\Delta_\mathrm{f}G^\circ = \Delta_\mathrm{f}H^\circ - T\,\Delta_\mathrm{f}S^\circ$ with $\Delta_\mathrm{f}S^\circ = S^\circ - \sum S^\circ_\mathrm{elements}$ (elements in their reference state).
\textit{Zn: Phase nicht angegeben: (cr) angenommen, die bei 298,15 K und 1 bar stabile Phase (kleinstes $\Delta$fG\textdegree{} unter (cr), (g))}
\textit{Cu: Phase nicht angegeben: (cr) angenommen, die bei 298,15 K und 1 bar stabile Phase (kleinstes $\Delta$fG\textdegree{} unter (cr), (g))}
For the extent $\xi = 0.09942$\,mol the heat of reaction at constant pressure is $Q = \xi\,\Delta_\mathrm{r}H^\circ = -21.02$\,kJ.
Titration of 25.0\,mL of the solution 0,1 M CH3COOH with NaOH ($c = 0.100$\,mol/L); dilution included, ideal dilute solution~\cite{er-harris,er-atkins,er-bandura2006}.

Suitable indicator at equivalence point: Thymol blue (transition 8.0--9.6, yellow to blue; titration error $0.00$\,\%); Phenolphthalein (transition 8.0--9.6, colourless to red; titration error $0.00$\,\%). Titration error = volume at the middle of the transition range minus the equivalence volume, relative to the equivalence volume~\cite{er-harris}.
